articles.title: Iran Braces for a Budget Without Oil Revenue
articles.description: Iran is drafting next year’s budget under the premise that oil revenue could fall to zero, with senior budget official Mohammad Ghasemi telling the government on Monday to prepare for that scenario, as the country appears to be weeks away from that eventuality. Iran has loaded no crude since August 25, according to the US Treasury, and the oil it held at sea outside the US blockade fell from 88.8 million barrels in mid-July to zero by mid-October. articles.description: Commercial crude oil stocks, not including the SPR, came in at 414.417 million barrels on November 6, the EIA's latest weekly petroleum status report revealed.

articles.title: ExxonMobil Greenlights Eighth Stabroek Project
articles.description: ExxonMobil announced a $12.5-billion final investment decision to proceed with Longtail - the first development that is primarily gas and condensate - in the Stabroek block offshore Guyana, after securing government approvals.

articles.description: Yesterday the US Senate approved a preliminary version of a bill, the Bipartisan Affordability and Jobs Act, commonly referred to as BAAJA. articles.title: Murphy Oil Re-Enters Cameroon
articles.description: Cameroon awarded Murphy Oil four production sharing contracts, marking the company's re-entry into the Central African country after exiting a decade ago.

articles.title: Trump Extends Jones Act Waiver For Another 90 Days
articles.description: President Donald Trump extended the Jones Act waiver for another 90 days on Friday, keeping foreign-flagged tankers eligible to move oil and other commodities between U.S. ports as the war with Iran continues to drive up fuel costs. The extension, confirmed by a White House official who spoke to Reuters, continues what is already the longest waiver in the shipping law's history. Foreign vessels will still need approval for individual voyages due to a restriction introduced in August after earlier blanket exemptions drew opposition from the domestic…

articles.title: Beijing Turns to Soft Power as Washington Expands Central Asia Ties
articles.description: China is responding to a successful US push to raise its trade profile in Central Asia by launching a far-reaching information campaign to sway hearts and minds in Central Asia’s most populous state. In late October and early November, CGTN, China’s international broadcaster operated by the Communist Party’s Central Propaganda Department, sponsored an unprecedented information campaign touting the PRC’s expansive ties with Uzbekistan. articles.description: The number of employees in the oil and gas extraction industry hit its lowest figure so far this year, data on the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics website showed.

articles.title: U.S. Oil Rig Count Holds at 463 as Crude Output Hits Another Record
articles.description: The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States fell this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Friday, with the total rig count in the US falling to 601, up 52 from this same time last year. The number of active oil rigs stayed the same at 463 during the latest reporting period, according to the data. This is 46 above this same time last year. articles.title: Iraq’s Oil Production Soars to 2019 High as Hormuz Flows Surge
articles.description: Iraq’s crude oil production hit 4.6 million barrels per day (bpd) in October, the highest since 2019, data from the International Energy Agency’s monthly report showed on Friday, as OPEC’s second-largest producer hiked output by 540,000 bpd from September. Kuwait and Saudi Arabia also boosted their October crude oil output compared to September, as rising volumes of oil are leaving the Strait of Hormuz on smaller tankers, which then transfer the crude cargoes onto supertankers in the Gulf of Oman. articles.title: Eni Plans Nearly $15B Gross Investment in UK through 2030
articles.description: Eni unveiled plans for around GBP 11 billion in 'gross investments' in the United Kingdom between 2026 and 2030, focused on lower-carbon projects.

articles.title: India's Road Fuel Demand Won't Peak Until 2034
articles.description: India’s fuel demand for road transportation is nearly a decade away from peaking despite rising sales of electric two- and three-wheelers, as commercial transport and conventional fleets will keep using greater volumes of gasoline and diesel, BloombergNEF has said. India’s fuel demand for road transportation is expected to peak at above 2.5 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2034, research firm BloombergNEF said in its India Electric Vehicle Outlook 2026. India’s rising road fuel demand could sustain global oil demand growth for…

articles.title: Germany Is Dismantling a Nord Stream Power Plant for Ukraine
articles.description: A power plant built at the landfall of the Nord Stream gas pipelines in northeastern Germany was shut down after the pipelines were sabotaged. Now the facility is being dismantled and sent to Ukraine. The Greifswald industrial power plant in Lubmin is majority owned by Germany’s Securing Energy for Europe (SEFE). Adrianne Montgobert, a spokesperson for the state-owned company, confirmed to RFE/RL that dismantling of the plant is currently under way, with its transfer being managed by a team from Naftogaz, Ukraine’s oil and gas giant.…

articles.title: SLB wins Vår Energi integrated drilling services deal on NCS
articles.description: Energy technology company SLB has been selected by Vår Energi as the main supplier of integrated drilling services for the Transocean Barents and Deepsea Bergen rigs operating on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS).

articles.title: Reliance plans $4.6bn investment in Andhra Pradesh coal-to-gas project
articles.description: Indian multinational conglomerate Reliance Industries has outlined plans to invest approximately Rs430bn ($4.57bn) in a facility to transform underground coal into gas in Andhra Pradesh, India, according to a government memorandum reviewed by Reuters.
